title: OOM diffuser and KV cache resynthesis runtime patch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + dedicated + private) reported cascading GPU OOMs during high-concurrency inference spikes. Root-cause analysis points to two cooperating failure modes: 1) uncontrolled KV cache growth of multi-tenant prefix state that retained tombstoned entries and prevented compaction; 2) a race in the async eviction path whereby stale slab pointers were briefly dereferenced, triggering allocator fragmentation and eventual allocation failures. The combined effect produces long-lived slab fragmentation and sudden per-node GPU allocation failures under bursty request distributions.
impact_details: Observed across environments: hosted burst clusters, several dedicated pools, and one customer private deployment during their nightly batch-generation window. Symptoms: sudden increase in gpu_alloc_failures (x10 baseline), slab_fragmentation_ratio rising above 0.82, sustained session_eviction_count spikes, degraded tail latency, and customer-facing errors (503 & spike in token generation stalls). Two customers opened escalations: Priority P0 (enterprise) and P1 (mid-market).
root_cause_summary: The async evictor deferred tombstone reclamation for performance; under specific request patterns this deferral prevented index compaction and allowed a pathological buildup of small fragmented allocations. Concurrently, an edge-case pointer reuse in the slab allocator allowed a freed slot to be briefly visible to another thread before metadata reconciliation, corrupting a small set of KV entries. The corruption delayed normal eviction heuristics, amplifying fragmentation and causing allocator refusal to satisfy large contiguous allocation requests required for certain GPU kernels (leading to OOM).
mitigation_applied: 1) Emergency: forced canary node drains in affected pools and tenant isolation for the two escalations to reduce contention. 2) Config change: reduced async-evict deferral window from 120s to 5s for affected clusters to accelerate tombstone reclamation. 3) Temporary safeguard: enabled per-tenant slab soft-quotas on hosted/dedicated to prevent single-tenant runaway growth. These mitigations reduced immediate OOM frequency but are stopgaps; a runtime patch is required.
proposed_fix: Introduce 'diffuser' background task that smooths KV cache growth by rate-limiting prefix allocation spikes and preemptively coalescing tombstones into a compacted shard off the hot path. Add a 'resynthesis' repair path: a lock-free index rebuild that can run incrementally to reconstruct a compact index snapshot while preserving live handles. Patch the slab allocator to insert an ephemeral write-fence on pointer handoff between threads to eliminate the observed dereference race. Ensure the resynthesis path writes a verified checksum and versioned journal to allow safe rollback if corruption detected.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): runtime-1.20.1-hotfix deploy to 3 canary nodes in hosted prod and 1 dedicated pool; monitor kv_index_compaction_rate, slab_fragmentation_ratio, gpu_alloc_failures_per_min for 24h. Stage 2 (gradual): expand to 25% of capacity with canary ramp and automatic rollback triggers on defined SLI regressions. Stage 3 (full): global rollout with telemetry retention and post-rollout audit. For private customers, offer controlled patch package and assisted upgrade window.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for write-fence and resynthesis journal; integration stress harness that replays the customer traffic pattern (bursty long-prefix sequences) to validate compaction and allocator stability; perf benchmarks to ensure median latency impact <5% and token-cost delta acceptable. Create an e2e scenario that simulates tombstone storm and verifies the diffuser reduces peak KV growth by >= 60%.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add new alerts: kv_resynthesis_failures > 0, slab_fragmentation_ratio > 0.75 sustained > 10m, gpu_alloc_failures_per_min > 5. Dashboards: per-tenant slab usage heatmap, kv_compaction_activity, diffuser_throttle_rate. Log enrichment: correlate tenant_id and session_id in allocator OOM traces for faster RCA.
rollback_plan: Hot rollback: flip runtime config flag to disable diffuser/resynthesis and revert write-fence to prior behavior (fast path) which restores prior perf profile. During rollback, enable aggressive eviction and tenant isolation until normal levels return.
open_questions: Do we enable resynthesis by default for all tenants or gate behind per-customer opt-in?
What's the acceptable latency budget for the diffuser under PLG free-tier customers?
Should we expose per-tenant slab quotas as self-serve controls in Console or keep server-side defaults for now?
updates: 2025-02-18: Incident triaged by on-call; Asha opened ticket; initial mitigation (tenant isolation + reduce evict deferral) applied to stop immediate OOMs.

2025-02-20: Heap & KV index dump analysis complete; repro harness created to mimic customer pattern (large prefix churn). Added ENG-214512 and ENG-61234 as technical dependencies for journaling and eviction heuristics.
2025-02-24: Prototype diffuser implemented; local stress tests show 65% reduction in peak KV growth but +3% median latency. Began write-fence implementation to harden pointer handoff.

2025-02-27: Security review scoped (no customer data leaked by resynthesis journal) — security_review_required set to false after signoff by Security. Draft PR submitted: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4218

2025-03-01: Canary deploy started on 3 hosted nodes and 1 dedicated pool; early telemetry shows slab_fragmentation_ratio falling and gpu_alloc_failures reduced to baseline on canaries. Monitoring thresholds tuned. Assigned to Liam for final patch notes and playbook updates.
followups: PM: update customer postmortems and SLO credit proposals
Docs: add runtime-1.20.1-hotfix release notes and operator upgrade guide
Design: consider Console UI for per-tenant slab quota visibility
notes: This ticket bundles a production hotfix and a longer-term runtime improvement. Keep communication channels open with the two escalated customers; schedule a dedicated upgrade window for the private deployment customer to apply the patch with SRE assistance.
